decisions.reason: As a newly launched flagship product line close to the core software business, Product A fits the firm's strategic direction and, with growth and likely organisational slack, would usually be retained unless results quickly fell well below aspiration.

Product B extends existing training and customer relationships, and in a growing firm with broad offerings it is likely to be kept while management learns about demand, though its more peripheral fit makes it somewhat more droppable than the flagship software line.

Product C directly supports the firm's established software and service activities, so under behavioral theory a growing firm with internal R&D and slack would normally keep it unless early usage clearly disappointed relative to aspirations.
